timeline.title: The field year
timeline.subtitle: Average month on this field, NASA POWER replay {{from}}–{{to}}. Filled cell = living crop, dashed cell = bare soil.
timeline.compoundNote: Share of years in which the month was both abnormally hot and abnormally dry (z > 1 against this field’s own {{from}}–{{to}} history). 2 of 4 signals: soil moisture and NDVI are not included yet. “–” = a normally dry month.
timeline.none: No heat + dry months in the record.
timeline.cellLive: {{share}}% of days with a living crop
timeline.compoundNote4: Rows show the share of years in which each month was abnormal (z > 1 against this field’s own {{from}}–{{to}} history). Compound stress = at least 3 of 4 signals abnormal together (heat, dryness, soil moisture, crop greenness); when a signal is undefined, all but one of the others. “–” = signal not meaningful in that month.
timeline.terrain: Terrain (NASADEM): mean slope {{slope}}°, steepest {{max}}°, elevation {{elev}} m.
timeline.ndviSource: Crop greenness: MODIS NDVI averaged over cropland only (ESA WorldCover 10 m; {{share}} % of the land within {{km}} km is cropland).
timeline.hidden: Hidden signals — what no single dataset shows
timeline.hiddenIntro: Fihrist compares crop greenness from space with the weather and soil water for the same month. When they disagree, the cause is probably not the climate. These are questions for the farmer, not conclusions.
timeline.unexplained: Crops weaker than the weather explains
timeline.unexplainedHint: Greenness far below normal (z > 1.5) while heat, rain and soil water were normal. Possible causes outside the climate record: canal water cut, late or failed sowing, pests, land-use change.
timeline.buffered: Crops green despite a dry month
timeline.bufferedHint: Rain or soil water far below normal, yet greenness at or above normal — the crops were buffered, most likely by irrigation.
timeline.satPresetsOnly: Satellite layers (crop greenness, soil moisture, slope) are prefetched for the four presets; for other points only the two weather signals are used (information gap).

charts.title: Ten years on this field
charts.soilNSub: Cumulative N fixed − N removed in harvests, kg N/ha (replay {{from}}–{{to}}). Losses are not modelled.
charts.waterSub: Water withdrawn per year, m³/ha (net need ÷ {{eff}} efficiency).
charts.waterRainfedSub: Crop water demand not covered by rain, m³/ha per year.
charts.uncertaintySub: P10–P90 across {{runs}} simulated 12-year futures; dot = P50.
charts.uncertaintyReplay: Range across rolling cycles {{from}}–{{to}} (Monte Carlo still running).
charts.noSpread: No spread: with full canal supply assumed, weather changes how much water the crops take, not the harvest. Water cuts are not modelled yet.

drawer.methodologyEnglish: The full methodology is in English: equations, data, and every parameter with its source and evidence level.
drawer.validationEnglish: The validation report is in English. It is computed live from the Kansas data with the same engine as the cards.

why.baseline: This is what you grow now. The other two rotations are compared against it.
why.waterSaving: Brings in chickpea, a legume that feeds the soil with nitrogen, and sorghum, a cereal that tolerates heat and dry spells.
why.regenerative: Adds a summer mung bean after the wheat harvest and a winter cover crop, so living roots protect and feed the soil most of the year.
why.lessWater: Uses {{pct}}% less water than your current rotation.
why.moreWater: Uses {{pct}}% more water than your current rotation — summer crops grow in the hottest, driest months.

evidence.climate: NASA POWER daily data for this point ({{from}}–{{to}}): yearly reference evapotranspiration {{et0}} mm, rain {{rain}} mm, July maximum {{tmax}} °C, {{frost}} frost days a year.
evidence.season: On 2015–2024 weather this rotation needed {{etc}} mm of crop water a year; effective rain supplied {{peff}} mm.
evidence.sources: Datasets: NASA POWER (MERRA-2 meteorology, CERES radiation). Method: FAO-56 Penman–Monteith, FAO-33 yield response.

benefit.profitNote: True profit = crop value minus the cost of replacing the nitrogen the crops removed. Other farm costs are not included.

gap.grid: NASA POWER cells are about 50 km wide (cell elevation {{elev}} m); a 1 ha field can be warmer, cooler or wetter.
gap.rainDoubt: Satellite-model rain can be too low in mountain valleys — check against a local rain gauge.
gap.soil: Soil water is modelled (FAO-56), but runoff, capillary rise and winter dormancy are not. In Kansas, modelled rainfed wheat yields follow real good and bad years but sit well below USDA averages, so rainfed food numbers are conservative (see Validation).
gap.nLoss: Nitrogen losses (leaching, gas) are not modelled, so the real nitrogen debt is likely larger.
gap.prices: Prices are international reference prices, not your local market.
gap.dormancy: Winter dormancy of wheat is not modelled yet (open question).
gap.region: Reference yields are for Central Asia and may not fit this location.
gap.params: {{n}} numbers here are proxies or not yet verified:

risk.seed: Is good seed of {{crops}} available and affordable locally?
risk.machinery: Small-seeded legumes may need different planting and harvesting equipment.
risk.water: Summer crops need irrigation turns in July–August — agree the schedule with your water-user association.
risk.market: Is there a buyer for {{crops}} at a fair price?
risk.pests: New crops bring new pests and diseases — plan field scouting with an agronomist.
risk.drought: In a dry year (P10) this rotation feeds {{p10}} people/ha instead of {{p50}}.
risk.nDebt: Soil nitrogen keeps falling: {{n}} kg N/ha over 10 years unless replaced with fertilizer or legumes.
risk.labour: Two crops a year means more work at harvest and sowing time.

grid.title: Fihrist Compute Grid
grid.how: Each future is 12 years assembled from real NASA POWER years 2001–2023 drawn at random; all three rotations face the same draws.
grid.cpuNote: Cloudflare Workers freeze timers during execution, so edge rows show round-trip time; local rows show measured worker time.

band.farmerIrr: In a dry decade (1 in 10) the canal water need rises to about {{water}} m³ a year.

editor.applied: Your rotation is used as the baseline.
editor.empty: Add at least one harvested crop.
editor.overlap: {{a}} (year {{ya}}) is still in the field when {{b}} (year {{yb}}) would be sown. Change one of them.
editor.dates: Sowing dates used: potato 1 Mar, chickpea 15 Mar, cotton 10 Apr, sorghum and maize 20 Apr, mung bean 20 Jun (after wheat), cover crop 5 Oct, wheat and barley 15 Oct (wheat 1 Nov after cotton). The cycle repeats.
